newsitem.title: JAPAN: No big rise in Japan surplus seen mid-term--MITI.
newsitem.headline: No big rise in Japan surplus seen mid-term--MITI.

text.p: Drastic increases in Japan's trade surplus are not likely in the medium term, Trade Minister Shinji Sato told a news conference on Tuesday.

He said that a large part of the dramatic increase in April's trade surplus was likely to have arisen from a fall-off in imports after the sales tax was increased on April 1 to five percent from three percent.
He added that Japan's trading patterns had changed so that structurally it was more difficult for exports to increase and imports to decrease.
If car exports continued to be strong until autumn, however, the United States was likely to complain and it would become difficult for Japan to explain surplus increases, he said.
Japan's trade surplus for April more than doubled from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen, according to finance ministry data released on Monday.
Sato said that it was problematic, however, to look at year-on-year comparisons of trade data and that it might be more appropriate to watch month-on-month comparisons.
He also said it was important to watch foreign exchange rates, which had a tendency to fluctuate.
